scams.name: The San Marco & "Calle Pickpocket" Rings
scams.description: Coordinated pickpocket teams — often women and minors — work Piazza San Marco, the Mercerie, Calle della Mandola (now tagged 'Calle Pickpocket' by activists) and the San Marco Vallaresso/San Zaccaria vaporetto imbarcaderi. Corriere del Veneto's October 25, 2025 investigation documents 200+ pickpockets caught in Venice in 2025 with 'none staying in jail more than a single night'; a Carabinieri maxi-inchiesta mapped 35 suspects, one ringleader ('Shakira,' 20-year-old Bosnian, 65 prior proceedings) demanding a €2,500-per-day haul from underlings including minors and pregnant women. A September 24, 2024 VeneziaToday case had an American tourist GPS-track his AirPods to a 13-year-old thief in Piazza San Marco.
scams.avoidance: Wear a crossbody bag with zipper to body and one hand on it in San Marco, Calle della Mandola, the Mercerie and all vaporetto gangways. Split cash, cards and passport across two places. Do not confront suspected thieves yourself — the July 19, 2025 Corriere del Veneto case of a German tourist wrongly beaten at San Zaccaria shows why; call polizia locale on 041 274 7070. Use Find My / Find My Device beforehand so a stolen phone is trackable.
scams.location: Piazza San Marco, Mercerie, Calle della Mandola, Frezzeria, San Marco Vallaresso and Santa Maria del Giglio imbarcaderi, Ponte di Rialto approaches

scams.name: The Ponte degli Scalzi Tre Scatolette Shell Game
scams.description: The Tre Scatolette (three shells) con clusters on Ponte degli Scalzi, Ponte delle Guglie and Ponte di Rialto approaches — the pedestrian bridges funnelling tourists from Santa Lucia onto the main island. ANSA July 6, 2024 documented a policy response: foglio di via obbligatorio expulsions tied to the scam jumped from 9 all of 2023 to 19 in just the first six months of 2024, with 115 violations vs. 17 the year before. VeneziaToday's 'Scatolettisti a Venezia, 9 denunciati' report documents the textbook Ponte degli Scalzi MO with a 30-year-old American tourist victim and nine Eastern European accomplices (including shills cheering fake winners).
scams.avoidance: Treat any three-shell or matchbox game on a Venice bridge as a guaranteed €100–€300 loss and walk past without eye contact. Never engage even to 'watch one round.' If a stranger points at the game and says 'easy money,' they are part of the ring. Report active games to polizia locale on 041 274 7070. Cross Ponte degli Scalzi with your bag closed and in front of you — the surrounding crowd is prime pickpocket territory even if you don't play.
scams.location: Ponte degli Scalzi, Ponte delle Guglie, Ponte di Rialto approaches, Strada Nova, Piazzale Roma-to-Santa Lucia corridor

scams.name: Marco Polo Water Taxi & Abusivo NCC Drivers
scams.description: Unlicensed water-taxi and NCC drivers meet arrivals at Marco Polo, quote inflated 'flat' fares, run 'broken' meters, or pick up tourists at Mestre FS forecourt. Il Gazzettino's market report counts 600 unlicensed operators against 300 regolari; a Guardia di Finanza sweep found 12 entirely unlicensed NCC drivers at Marco Polo and sanctioned 46 more (VeneziaToday). A Mestre-station abusivo was fined €25,000 for running private-car 'taxi' rides to Venice hotels (Il Gazzettino). The legitimate Consorzio Motoscafi Marco Polo–San Marco water-taxi fare is roughly €120–€140 for up to 4 passengers.
scams.avoidance: Take the Alilaguna airport waterbus (~€15) to San Marco/Rialto or the ATVO/ACTV bus (~€10) to Piazzale Roma from Marco Polo — both at posted signed counters in arrivals. For private water taxi, use only the Consorzio Motoscafi rank at the Darsena and confirm the posted flat fare before boarding. Never follow a driver who approaches inside the terminal. At Mestre or Piazzale Roma, use only official white taxis with visible TAXI roof sign. Pay by card to log the transaction.
scams.location: Venezia Marco Polo Airport (VCE), Darsena water taxi dock, Mestre FS forecourt, Piazzale Roma taxi rank

scams.name: The San Marco Restaurant Maxi-Conto
scams.description: Restaurants off Piazza San Marco stack unmarked coperto, automatic servizio, unordered pane/acqua/antipasti, and fish/steak priced 'al etto' (per 100g) to produce runaway bills. The textbook case: a January 2018 Osteria in the Mercerie charged four Japanese tourists €1,143 for four bistecche and a fritto misto, triggering a €20,000 Comune di Venezia fine (Repubblica, January 24, 2018); VeneziaToday flagged a parallel €350 three-pasta lunch for Japanese tourists the same week. An August 18, 2025 Repubblica Il Gusto piece documents an €81 bill for 4 Cokes, 2 beers and 2 coffees at a San Marco view-bar ('prezzi chiari, vista super').
scams.avoidance: Photograph the posted outside menu with prices visible before you sit — Italian law requires it. At seating ask 'mi conferma il coperto, il servizio e i prezzi del pesce al etto?' Walk 10 minutes off the San Marco–Rialto axis — Cannaregio (Fondamenta della Misericordia), Dorsoduro (Campo Santa Margherita), Santa Croce and the Giudecca are the real-eating zones. Trust Italian-language Google reviews sorted by Most Recent. Demand a scontrino fiscale; no receipt, no pay.
scams.location: Osterie/trattorie on the Mercerie, Calle Vallaresso, Frezzeria; view-bars facing Bacino San Marco and the Canal Grande

scams.name: Fake Vaporetto Ticket Sellers at Ferrovia
scams.description: Strangers near ACTV machines at Ferrovia, Piazzale Roma and Ponte degli Scalzi sell tourists fake, resident-only, or used vaporetto tickets — triggering on-board fines of ~€60 when inspectors check. VeneziaToday documented the scheme in October 2016: a ring bought €1.50 resident ACTV tickets and resold them for €6+ (today's ACTV adult single is €9.50 for 75 minutes). The modern variant exploits ACTV tap-and-go rollout confusion — 2024 Venice community threads note charges appear days late and inspectors require the last four digits of the tapping card, which scammers exploit. ACTV explicitly warns tickets must come only from ACTV/AVM machines or AVM-logo tobacconists.
scams.avoidance: Buy only at official ACTV/AVM machines (blue-circle logo) at Ferrovia, Piazzale Roma, San Marco Vallaresso, Rialto, Lido, or Marco Polo. For 2–7 day stays, the Venezia Unica Travel Card (24/48/72h/7-day) at the Santa Lucia kiosk or veneziaunica.it is best value. For tap-and-go, keep the tapping card handy for inspector checks. Always validate paper tickets at the yellow imbarcadero reader before boarding. Report bad tickets at the polizia anti-scam stand on the piazzale in front of Santa Lucia.
scams.location: Santa Lucia station (Ferrovia), Piazzale Roma, Ponte degli Scalzi, the station-to-vaporetto pedestrian approach

scams.name: Gondola Price Gouging Above the €90 Official Rate
scams.description: The Comune di Venezia publishes a fixed Ente Gondola tariff: €90 for 30 min daytime (8am–7pm), €110 for 30 min evening (7pm–8am), €45 per additional 20 min day, €55 per 20 min evening — one fare for up to 5 passengers. A widely-circulated Reddit/YouTube case ('Gondolas in Venice: $80 for 30 minutes') documented a London group charged ~£206 (~€240) for a 10-minute ride; the gondolier backed down only after bystanders filmed the dispute. Scam forms: verbal 'flat' quotes above the published rate; clock not starting at boarding; 'music/singing' surcharges not disclosed; 20-minute rides billed at the 40-minute price.
scams.avoidance: Before boarding, confirm verbally: 'trenta minuti, novanta euro, vero?' and get an explicit yes. Start your phone stopwatch the moment the gondolier pushes off; 30 minutes is 30 minutes. Ride from an official stazi (Bacino Orseolo, San Tomà, Santa Maria del Giglio) rather than a mobile pickup. For a €2 alternative, take a traghetto (standing gondola ferry) across the Canal Grande at one of seven crossing points. If overcharged, demand a ricevuta and report to comune.venezia.it.
scams.location: Gondola stazi at Bacino Orseolo, San Marco, San Tomà, Santa Maria del Giglio, Rialto, Santa Sofia, San Moisè; non-stazi pickups near Bridge of Sighs

scams.name: Fake "Made in Murano" Glass Souvenirs
scams.description: Counterfeit 'Murano' glass floods San Marco souvenir shops and many shops on Murano itself without a working fornace. A Guardia di Finanza di Venezia sweep documented by Il Gazzettino seized 180,000+ counterfeit items in a single operation including fake Murano pearls and glass. Local glass-workers' verdict from Venice community forums: 'Half of the places listed are scam… if they don't have equipment for making things in the shop, it's probably not worth your time.' Sub-variants include 'free tour to Murano' commission boats, shop-printed fake 'certificates,' and San Marco stalls selling made-in-China imitation masks and pendants. The only legal mark is the trademarked Vetro Artistico Murano gold serial-numbered sticker.
scams.avoidance: Buy on Murano at a fornace where you can see glass being blown — take ACTV 4.1/4.2 vaporetto to Murano Colonna or Murano Faro. Look for the Vetro Artistico Murano gold sticker with a serial number; without it, you cannot prove origin. Prefer family names locally vouched for (e.g. Schiavon) or large cooperatives on Fondamenta dei Vetrai. Refuse 'free' hotel/street-agent Murano boats; ride the regular vaporetto from Fondamente Nove. Pay by card for chargeback protection.
scams.location: Souvenir shops on the Mercerie, around Piazza San Marco, Strada Nova, Rialto Mercato; also Murano island shops without a visible fornace

scams.name: The Off-Platform Hotel Payment Switch
scams.description: After booking a Venice hotel on Booking.com or Airbnb, travelers receive messages (often within minutes) asking them to pay on an external Italian website — a direct T&Cs violation and a common fraud vector. A 2025 traveler forum thread documents a Venice hotel sending exactly this request minutes after a Booking.com reservation; the top reply confirms 'this is an almost-scam… do not do this.' An ANSA March 24, 2026 report notes Jesolo launched Italy's first anti-scam registry for short-term-rental locations after the extralberghiero sector hit 1.2 million overnights in 2025. A separate ANSA November 2024 report flags fake QR codes for the €5 Venice day-tripper access fee. Venice's real tassa di soggiorno is €1–€5 per person per night by hotel class.
scams.avoidance: Pay only through the booking platform you started on; never click external payment links. Screenshot off-platform requests and report to Booking.com or Airbnb — they actively police this and refund. Budget the €5/day Venice contributo d'accesso only on official red-circle days via cda.ve.it — never via a QR code from a host or street agent. Confirm your tassa di soggiorno at booking time; it should appear on your stay invoice. Prefer hotels with 100+ reviews and a visible sestiere street-number on Google Street View.
scams.location: Hotel and short-term rental listings in San Marco, Cannaregio, Dorsoduro, Santa Croce, near Santa Lucia; also Lido, Mestre and Marghera
